_: Otters are classified as restricted species under California Code of Regulations §671, and possession is not allowed without a permit issued by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife.
Otters are regulated wildlife in Florida. Possession requires a Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) permit under Chapter 379 (personal possession of wildlife).
River otters may only be possessed, transported, or disposed of as permitted by regulations of the Department of Environmental Conservation (NY Environmental Conservation Law §11-0917).

River otters are classified as furbearers, and it is unlawful to possess a live otter taken from the wild without first securing a permit from a Pennsylvania Game Commission officer, meaning possession is restricted and permit-based rather than general private ownership.

River otters are classified as wildlife, and private ownership is not allowed unless a special permit is issued by the Ohio Department of Natural Resources for limited purposes such as education, research, or rehabilitation.

River otters are classified as furbearer wildlife, and it is unlawful to import, possess, or transport them without a state permit, which may only be issued after approval by the Department of Natural Resources for specific regulated purposes.
River otters require a Michigan Department of Natural Resources “Permit to Hold Game in Captivity” for possession in captivity.
All Mustelidae species (weasels, badgers, skunks, and otters) are non-native (exotic) animals require a special permit to import, possess, or sell under 4VAC15-30-40(A).
In Arizona, live wildlife generally cannot be possessed unless a special license or lawful exemption is granted, because "restricted live wildlife" explicitly requires a permit for possession.
River otters are classified as wildlife, and private possession as pets is prohibited except under Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency permits for authorized purposes.

River otters are classified as a furbearer (wildlife species), and private possession as a pet is not allowed; they may only be possessed under Indiana Department of Natural Resources permits for licensed purposes.
River otters are classified as wildlife (furbearers), and possession is prohibited except with specific state permit authorization.

Otters are designated fur-bearing animals, and possession of a live otter beyond trap conditions requires a permit from the Alabama Department of Conservation and Natural Resources unless otherwise authorized.

It is unlawful to breed, possess or raise native wildlife (including river otters as “native wildlife”) without first obtaining a commercial wildlife breeder’s license from the Director, meaning possession is restricted and requires a state-issued license/permit under Oklahoma…
River otters are classified as wildlife, and possession is prohibited unless authorized by the Nevada Department of Wildlife.

River otters are classified as furbearer wildlife, and private possession as pets is not allowed; possession is only permitted under Nebraska Game and Parks Commission authorization (typically for licensed wildlife purposes).

River otters are classified as non-domestic mammals and require a state-issued possession permit (or zoo permit for exhibitors), meaning they cannot be kept as private pets without authorization under the South Dakota permit system.

River otters are classified as Category 2 non-traditional livestock, meaning they are regulated wildlife and require state licensure and (in some cases) a Permit to Possess, Propagate, or Domesticate, so they cannot be kept as ordinary private pets.
